subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical exec review inputs within one reviewer/run, and should the cache include only allow-once results or all parsed ask/error/timeout outcomes?
rationale: The repeated billing defect is source-proven, but exec auto-review sits on the process approval boundary, so one-request-one-review semantics should not change without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve exact-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and keep allow-once consumption single-use at the host boundary.

options.title: Narrow cached outcomes
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once decisions and keep ask, timeout, and error outcomes uncached for a smaller approval-boundary change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Reject memoization and accept repeated reviewer cost to preserve a fresh model review for every exec request.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and keep allow-once consumption single-use at the host boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent exec approval history make vincentkoc the strongest available owner for the approval-boundary cache decision.
